chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not strike the animals upon their faces, for they glorify with the praise of Allah.' He said, and in another hadith: 'Do not brand them in their faces.'

key_terms.الدَّوَابَّ: al-dawabb — beasts of burden, working animals (horses, donkeys, mules); broader meaning: all animals
key_terms.تَسِمُوهَا: tasimuha — to brand or mark with a hot iron; a common practice in early Arabia for identifying livestock
key_terms.تُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِ اللَّهِ: tusabbihu bi-hamdillah — they glorify Allah with praise; a Quranic motif indicating that all creation worships Allah (cf. 17:44, 24:41)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about striking animals on their faces in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWA) commands believers to refrain from striking or branding animals on their faces. The theological basis given is profound: animals actively glorify Allah (tasbih), making their faces sacred in a spiritual sense. This teaching reflects the Shia Islamic understanding that all of creation participates in the worship of Allah, and harming those engaged in His glorification is a violation of divine order. The hadith is transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) via Muhammad ibn Muslim, one of the most prominent companions of the Imams.
